purpose: Test whether the colophon works as an editorially coherent account of how the portfolio is made, reviewed, and maintained.

pageBrief.audience: A hiring reader, collaborator, or peer who wants to understand how the portfolio is composed and governed.
pageBrief.readerJob: Understand the relationship among Jamie's working knowledge, the selective public portfolio, its visual system, and its editorial safeguards without needing repository context.
requiredIdeas: The portfolio is a selective public rendering of a larger working system.
The source, evidence, and semantic graphs remain distinct before an audience-specific projection is composed.
Modeled editorial review produces critique and a binary result without replacing human publication authority.
The page identifies the site's writing, typography, photography, delivery, privacy, and maintenance choices.

allowedInputs: the exact rendered colophon beginning at /colophon
the page brief in this contract
the assigned owner's listed public sources
execution.disclaimer: Fictionalized analytical lenses informed by public work. These are not quotations, participation claims, approvals, endorsements, or predictions by the real people named.

owners.name: Deborah Treisman
owners.task: Evaluate only whether the colophon selects and orders its material into a lucid, proportionate narrative for a reader with no prior context.
owners.criterion: The page explains what the portfolio is, how its deeper system relates to the public selection, and why its safeguards matter without repetition, throat-clearing, or technical inventory overwhelming the story.

definitions.pass: A first-time reader can state the page's central idea, follow its sequence, and distinguish essential method from supporting production detail without rereading.
definitions.fail: The page is diffuse, repetitive, over-defensive, or organized as an inventory whose details obscure its central editorial argument.

developmentExamples.label: clear-pass
developmentExamples.inputSummary: The page opens with its purpose, explains the three-graph-to-publication relationship once, names the review responsibility, and moves concise production details to the end.

developmentExamples.label: clear-fail
developmentExamples.inputSummary: The page begins with a long tool list, repeats the same safety language in every section, and never explains why the system matters to a reader.

developmentExamples.label: borderline-fail
developmentExamples.inputSummary: The ideas are accurate, but every paragraph carries equal weight and the reader cannot tell what to remember.

outputSchema.critique: A concrete narrative assessment citing visible page evidence.
outputSchema.recommendedRevision: The smallest useful editorial change, or no revision needed.

owners.acceptanceStatement: The colophon passes the narrative selection and editorial proportion gate.

owners.name: Maggie Appleton
owners.task: Evaluate only whether the colophon makes the relationship among working knowledge, graph layers, editorial projection, and ongoing maintenance intuitive and inspectable.
owners.criterion: The page makes the source, evidence, and semantic graphs distinct; explains that the portfolio is an audience-specific projection; and shows how the site can evolve without presenting automation as truth or authority.

definitions.pass: A first-time reader can reconstruct the source-to-evidence-to-meaning-to-projection flow and identify where human review remains responsible.
definitions.fail: The page presents a vague digital garden, a magical AI pipeline, or a stack description without a comprehensible knowledge flow and correction boundary.

developmentExamples.label: clear-pass
developmentExamples.inputSummary: The page names all three graph roles, distinguishes them from the public projection, and makes review, correction, and maintenance human responsibilities.

developmentExamples.label: clear-fail
developmentExamples.inputSummary: The page says an AI knowledge graph automatically turns every source into a truthful public page.

developmentExamples.label: borderline-fail
developmentExamples.inputSummary: The page names three graphs but leaves their different responsibilities and the transition to publication unexplained.

outputSchema.critique: A concrete systems-legibility assessment citing visible page evidence.
outputSchema.recommendedRevision: The smallest useful systems explanation change, or no revision needed.

owners.acceptanceStatement: The colophon passes the living knowledge-system legibility gate.

owners.name: Ellen Lupton
owners.task: Evaluate only whether typography, hierarchy, spacing, and sequence make the colophon's editorial argument visible and readable across desktop and mobile.
owners.criterion: The visual hierarchy distinguishes thesis, method, review practice, and production notes; maintains readable measure and contrast; and uses the portfolio's material language without turning every section into the same visual unit.

definitions.pass: A reader can scan the page's hierarchy, settle into comfortable prose, and understand the relationship among sections before reading every sentence.
definitions.fail: Type, spacing, repetition, contrast, or responsive composition flatten the hierarchy, strain reading, or make the page's visual form contradict its editorial claims.

developmentExamples.label: clear-pass
developmentExamples.inputSummary: The page uses a strong title, a concise lead, varied but coherent section structures, readable line lengths, and restrained rules to guide the eye.

developmentExamples.label: clear-fail
developmentExamples.inputSummary: Every idea appears in an identical card, body lines span the viewport, secondary text lacks contrast, and headings wrap awkwardly on mobile.

developmentExamples.label: borderline-fail
developmentExamples.inputSummary: The typography is attractive, but the page's repeated two-column sections make unlike ideas look editorially equivalent.

outputSchema.critique: A concrete visual and typographic assessment citing visible page evidence.
outputSchema.recommendedRevision: The smallest useful design change, or no revision needed.

owners.acceptanceStatement: The colophon passes the typography, hierarchy, and form-content gate.
